item.title: Her Death Was Ruled Natural. He Killed Two More Women.
item.description: Police found Sally White dead in Anthony Hardy’s London flat in January 2002, but her death was attributed to natural causes. He murdered two more women that December. Hardy pleaded guilty to all three murders in 2003 and later received a whole-life order.

item.title: She Turned Off The Alarm And Let Her Parents’ Killers In
item.description: Suzane von Richthofen helped plan her parents’ 2002 murders in São Paulo, disabling security and admitting her boyfriend and his brother. Convicted in 2006 and sentenced to 39 years and six months, she was allowed to serve the remainder outside prison under court conditions in 2023.

item.title: A Basement Repair Exposed The Ice Cream Shop Murders
item.description: Workers making repairs in 2011 discovered two men’s remains concealed in concrete beneath Estibaliz Carranza’s Vienna ice cream shop. She confessed to killing her ex-husband and boyfriend in separate attacks and was sentenced to life imprisonment in 2012.

item.title: The Wife Swap Son Who Killed His Mother And Brother
item.description: The Stockdales appeared on “Wife Swap” in 2008, showcasing their strict household and family band. Nine years later, Jacob Stockdale killed his mother, Kathryn, and brother, James, at their Ohio home. He pleaded guilty to both murders in 2021 and received 30 years to life.

item.title: Police Checked On Him But Never Watched His Videos
item.description: Weeks before Elliot Rodger killed six people in Isla Vista, California, in May 2014, deputies checked on the 22-year-old over concerns about his online videos. Officials later confirmed they had not watched them. Rodger died by suicide after the attacks.

item.title: He Set His House On Fire To Frame His Ex
item.description: Mick Philpott planned to rescue his children from a deliberately set fire and blame his former girlfriend. Instead, six children died in the Derby blaze in May 2012. Convicted of six counts of manslaughter, he received a life sentence with a minimum term of 15 years.

item.title: His Toolbox Held Photos Of The Women He Killed
item.description: Harvey Glatman was arrested in California in 1958 after an officer found Lorraine Vigil fighting him for a gun. He confessed to three murders, and police discovered victims’ photographs in his toolbox. He pleaded guilty to two murders and was sentenced to death.

item.title: He Married The Woman He Had Raised As His Daughter
item.description: Franklin Delano Floyd abducted Suzanne Sevakis as a child, raised her under false identities and later married her. After her suspicious death in Oklahoma in 1990, it took investigators 24 years—and DNA testing—to establish her real name.
